# Notes

> Short, data-driven analyses on topics that matter for Switzerland.

Source: https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/ · Publisher: The Future (Swiss political party, Basel)

- [Artificial General Intelligence and the Labour Market: Two Scenarios for Switzerland](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/agi-szenarien-arbeitsmarkt/) (2026-11-08): How exposed Swiss occupations are to generative AI, how quickly the effects could arrive, and what transition policy a slow or a fast trajectory would require. Scenarios, not forecasts.
- [From 16th to 26th: Why Switzerland Is Falling Behind in E-Government](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/egovernment-rang-26/) (2026-11-08): In the UN E-Government Development Index, Switzerland fell from 16th (2020) to 23rd (2022) and 26th (2024). Infrastructure and education are strong; the gap lies in the state's online services.
- [Compute and Electricity: What Ten Times More Public AI Capacity Would Require](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/rechenkraft-und-strom/) (2026-11-08): In 2024 data centres used around 2.1 TWh, or 3.6% of Swiss electricity. By our estimate, a tenfold increase in public compute based on Alps would require 0.6 to 0.8 TWh per year: manageable with planning, but not as an afterthought.
- [Doubling Robot Density: What 600 Instead of 294 Robots Would Mean](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/roboterdichte-verdoppeln/) (2026-11-08): Switzerland has 294 industrial robots per 10,000 employees, fewer than Germany or Japan. Research shows that more robots raise productivity. Whether jobs are lost depends heavily on how the transition is organised.
- [Talent Visas Compared: Singapore, Hong Kong, the United Kingdom and Switzerland](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/talentvisa-im-vergleich/) (2026-11-08): Singapore, Hong Kong and the United Kingdom have dedicated routes for top talent: without a job offer or with a clear salary threshold, a decision in around four weeks, family included. Switzerland has only the general quota procedure.
- [Transparent by Law: 20 Years of the Freedom of Information Principle in Figures](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/transparent-per-gesetz/) (2026-11-08): Access requests to the federal administration have more than tripled since 2015. In 2025, however, full access was granted in only 39% of cases, and the number of statutory exemptions is growing.
- [Automation: How AI Is Shifting the Risk Map](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/automatisierungsrisiko-branchen/) (2026-02-12): LLM-capable AI changes automation risk: office jobs are more exposed, manual work less so.
- [The Digital Readiness Gap: The Population Is Online — the State Is Not](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/digitale-souveraenitaet-luecke/) (2026-02-12): 90% of Swiss residents use the internet, but e-government and open data lag behind the EU average. The problem is not technological — it is institutional.
- [Electricity Stress Test: What Happens with Drought plus a Nuclear Phase-Out?](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/energieresilienz-stressszenarien/) (2026-02-12): Four scenarios show how vulnerable Switzerland's electricity supply is — from the baseline to the worst case of drought combined with a nuclear shutdown.
- [Research: Who Does It, Who Pays — and What Comes Back?](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/forschung-wer-forscht-wer-zahlt/) (2026-02-12): Switzerland leads the world in R&D per capita and patent efficiency. But the private sector dominates — and the question of the public return on public research remains open.
- [Health Costs: Where Does the Money Go — and Where Does It Drain Away?](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/gesundheitskosten-verwaltung-fokus/) (2026-02-12): Switzerland spends 5.2% of health expenditure on administration — well above the OECD average. The excess costs ~CHF 10 per person per month.
- [Basic Income: Three Financing Models Compared](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/grundeinkommen-finanzierungsmodelle/) (2026-02-12): What happens to the income distribution if a UBI is financed through income tax, replacement of transfers or a consumption tax? A decile simulation with FSO data.
- [Rent Burden: When Does It Become Critical in Which Canton?](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/mietbelastung-kantonale-prognose/) (2026-02-12): The bottom quintile spends 40% on rent. On current trends, more cantons will cross the 30% threshold.
- [Talent & Migration: Are Qualifications Being Used — or Wasted?](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/talent-ueberqualifikation/) (2026-02-12): 36% of third-country nationals work below their level of qualification. This is not an integration failure — it is a loss of value added.
- [Defence: What Does the Swiss Defence Franc Buy?](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/verteidigung-ausgaben-prioritaeten/) (2026-02-12): Switzerland spends 0.706% of GDP on defence. 58% goes on personnel — but the population wants cyber defence and disaster relief.
- [Continuing Education: Who Takes Part — and Who Does Not?](https://die-zukunft.ch/en/zukunftslabor/notizen/weiterbildung-teilnahme-luecken/) (2026-02-12): The gap in continuing education is huge: highly qualified people take part 2.6× more often than those with low qualifications. The most exposed industries in particular invest too little.
